editorial.headline: Postsecondary Learning Beyond the Tertiary Boundary
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers general and vocational education after secondary school that remains outside tertiary education, with a nationally open foreign-ownership setting and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Postsecondary education does not automatically mean tertiary education. This activity covers the provision of general or vocational learning after secondary school where the programme remains outside the tertiary category. Its scope includes postsecondary non-tertiary education and training through both general and vocational pathways. It can also include additional postsecondary programmes that prepare learners for higher education, as well as vocational education and training at the same non-tertiary level. The defining point is therefore both the stage of learning and the classification of the programme: it follows secondary education, but it is not tertiary education.

The record opens this activity to micro, small, medium, and large scales. That matters because the classification is framed around the educational provision itself, rather than reserving the activity for one size of operator. Within its stated boundary, the activity can encompass general programmes, vocational programmes, and additional preparatory education for learners moving towards higher education. It also expressly accommodates non-tertiary postsecondary vocational education and training, keeping the vocational route within the same overall educational level.

Nationally, the activity is recorded as open to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. In practical terms, the record presents a fully open national ownership setting for this activity: foreign participation may reach the stated 100% ceiling. That national position should be read alongside the actual scope of the activity, which remains confined to postsecondary programmes that do not fall within tertiary education.

Bali does not add a moratorium block for this activity in the record. Its Bali status is recorded as OK or higher risk, with the reason identifying the activity as medium-high risk and therefore not blocked by the moratorium; verification remains necessary for the specific address. The Bali moratorium described in the record applies island-wide and permanently to low- and medium-low-risk PMA activities. For this activity, the honest position is more straightforward: it is nationally open, and it is not recorded as blocked for PMA registration in Bali under that moratorium, subject to address-specific verification.
